themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: Focuses on AI agents that can perform research tasks autonomously or with minimal human intervention, often involving multi-agent systems and complex workflows.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Covers AI tools and research that assist in writing, debugging, and refactoring code, improving developer productivity and code quality.

themes.name: AI research tools
themes.description: Encompasses a broad range of AI-powered platforms and tools designed to aid researchers in various stages of their work, from data analysis to literature review.

themes.name: AI research platforms
themes.description: Details platforms specifically built to facilitate and accelerate AI research, often offering integrated tools for experimentation, model development, and collaboration.

themes.name: AI testing automation
themes.description: Explores the use of AI to automate various aspects of software testing, including test case generation, execution, and analysis of results.

themes.name: AI design & research
themes.description: Covers the application of AI in the design process, from ideation and prototyping to generating design assets and informing research strategies.

themes.name: AI workforce impact
themes.description: Analyzes the effects of AI on employment, including job displacement, creation, skill requirements, and the future of work.

themes.name: Synthetic users
themes.description: Discusses the creation and use of synthetic data or virtual user personas for training AI models and conducting research without relying on real user data.

themes.name: AI customer insights
themes.description: Focuses on how AI is used to gather, analyze, and interpret customer data to understand behavior, preferences, and sentiment.

themes.name: AI content generation
themes.description: Covers AI tools and techniques for creating various forms of content, including text, images, and code.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
